statements.notes: The change has to be named exactly 'issue'.
statements.quote: the issue becomes an OpenSpec change named `issue`

statements.notes: The change goes through planning, apply, verify and archive in that order.
statements.quote: planned in artifacts, implemented, verified and archived

statements.notes: Every step is done through the openspec CLI.
This has to be the first action in the session. /opsx sits outside /testbed.
statements.quote: Make opening /opsx/core-workflow.md your very first action.

statements.notes: Follow the order given in core-workflow.md.
statements.quote: Take the actions in the order that file gives.

statements.notes: Read the stage document when entering each stage.
statements.quote: On entering one, read its stage document in /opsx/stages/

statements.notes: Each stage starts with the openspec command its stage document names.
statements.quote: begin from the `openspec` command it names
statements.target: openspec command named in stage doc

statements.notes: Go by the paths, artifact order and instructions the CLI returns.
statements.quote: what the CLI returns (paths, artifact order, instructions) beats assumptions
Write assumptions into the change's artifacts rather than asking

statements.notes: Don't ask the user for clarification.
statements.quote: Nobody replies before the task ends. ... rather than asking

statements.notes: No turn may contain only text.
statements.quote: keep every progress note in a turn that also calls a tool

statements.notes: finish has to come after the archive step is complete.
statements.quote: call finish only once the archive step is done
